NIGHT_THREATS: Numbers triple after dark and they gain darkvision.
At night the parasites take over and they coordinate like a single organism.
Dormant by day; at night they hunt in packs led by a Level +5 alpha.
day
Sunset triggers a frenzy; they attack anything, including each other.
After dark they go quiet and stalk. You won't hear them.
At night they retreat to nests and the region's real predator comes out.
night
They light fires at night. Follow the glow only if you want a fight.
Night doubles their level and halves their loot.
They sleep in heaps after dark and post one sentry. The sentry is the dangerous one.
Their eyes reflect torchlight at two hundred yards. So do yours, to them.
After sunset they will not cross running water, and they know where all of it is.
Night makes them cold-blooded and slow. It also makes them very hard to kill.
They sing at night. It carries for miles and it is a headcount.
At night they bury themselves and strike from underfoot.
Their camouflage only works in daylight. After dark they are obvious, and furious about it.
They hunt by body heat after dark, so a cold camp is genuinely invisible to them.
Night brings their young out, and the adults become considerably less reasonable.
After dark they will trade. By daylight they deny it ever happened.
They migrate at night, in one direction, and trample whatever is in the way.
Moonlight burns them. The overcast nights are the bad ones.
At night their wounds close. Anything done to them during the day is undone by dawn.
They drag the day's dead back to a cache after dark. Follow them if you want the gear.
Nightfall splits them into pairs that hunt a quarter mile apart.
After dark they mimic voices they heard during the day, including yours.
They go blind at night and compensate by being everywhere at once.
At night the whole region's worth of them converges on whatever is making light.
Territorial by day, nomadic by night. The map is wrong after sunset.
Night doubles their speed and halves their caution.
After dark they are docile unless touched, and they are difficult not to touch.
They take the high ground at night and throw things from it.
At night they stop eating and start collecting. They will take gear over food.
Their venom is only active after dark, which nobody warns a new crawler about.
They post no sentries at night, because something else is watching for them.
After dark they coordinate with the region next door, so clearing one achieves nothing.
At night there are three times as many of them and they are a third as brave.
They go quiet a full hour before dark. That hour is the only warning.
Night turns them scavenger; they will not start a fight they can inherit.
They roost at height after sunset and drop on whatever passes beneath.
After dark they follow sound rather than sight, and they are patient about it.
They do not exist in daylight. Not asleep, not hidden - gone, and back at dusk.
day
Strictly nocturnal; by day the region belongs to something else entirely.
day
They hatch at dusk and are dead by dawn, every night, without fail.
day
Daylight drives them underground, and what uses the surface is not related to them.
day
They bed down in a heap at sunset, and something else takes the region until dawn.
night
At dusk they run for the settlements, and whatever they are running from moves in.
night
By night they are prey rather than predator, and their predator is on this map.
night
They hold the region while the sun is up and surrender it at dusk without a fight.
night
RUIN_FEATURES: A signpost pointing to the nearest settlement. Half the signs lie.
A crashed circus wagon, cages open.
A public restroom that still works. Guarded by nothing. Suspicious.
An abandoned shrine to an Old God; offerings still fresh.
A fog bank that never lifts. Minimap goes dark inside it.
A collapsed bridge; the detour adds hours.
A crawler graveyard with names carved in three scripts.
A working fountain. The water is fine. Probably.
A gallows with a fresh notice: crimes and the crawler executed for them.
Ruined guildhall; the training dummies still animate.
A carnival calliope playing slowly, somewhere in the fog.
A rooftop route that avoids the streets, if you can climb.
A river crossing with a ferryman who takes payment in stories.
A field of standing stones, warm to the touch.
A watchtower, intact, manned by something that waves back.
An orchard still fruiting, the ground beneath it picked clean.
A caravan circled for the night, fires cold, nobody inside the ring.
A rope bridge over a gorge, one plank in three missing.
A hot spring that heals slowly and attracts everything within a mile.
A toppled statue of something the locals still leave food for.
A beehive the size of a cottage, humming in time with something.
A dry riverbed full of bones, sorted by size.
A hunter's blind overlooking a game trail that is still in use.
A boundary wall running for miles with no gate and no corner.
A grove where nothing grows but the trees, and the trees lean inward.
A mill with the wheel still turning and no water in the race.
A sinkhole with stairs cut into its wall, going down.
A roadside gibbet, the cage empty, the lock cut from the inside.
A plague marker fencing off a village that looks fine from here.
A trapper's line of snares, all sprung, all empty.
A quarry flooded to the brim, the equipment still on its shelf.
A shepherd's hut stocked for one person for a year.
A canopy walkway strung between trees, maintained by somebody.
A clearing with a single chair in the middle of it, facing the trail.
A termite mound taller than a house, carved with doors.
A salt flat that rings underfoot and holds a footprint for a week.
A stand of trees felled in one direction, all at once.
An aqueduct carrying clean water somewhere nobody has found.
A pilgrim's rest with a visitor's book and no recent entries.
A dead god's footprint, filled with rain and fish.
A boundary of hung charms the local mobs will not cross.
A burnt-out camp, fire pit still warm, tracks leading nowhere.
A tree with doors in it, each opening onto the same room.
A sunken road, banks higher than a man, perfect for an ambush.
A marsh with a causeway of stepping stones, one of them a back.
A vineyard gone to rot, the press full, the smell carrying for miles.
An obelisk listing names, adding one as you watch.
A ranger station with a map wall and every route crossed out but one.
QUEST_GIVER_ROLE: banker who has run out of patience
QUEST_OBJECTIVE: Retrieve the {item} from {region}.
Kill the {mob} that have been taking citizens from the outskirts.
Escort a caravan to {settlement} before nightfall.
Find out what happened to the patrol that went into {region}.
Recover the body of {giver}'s {relative} from {region}.
Deliver a sealed letter to {settlement}. Do not open it.
Clear the {mob} nest blocking the road to {region}.
Prove the {role} is innocent of the murders in the {settlement} slums.
Bring back proof the {mob} boss is dead.
Steal the {item} back from {region}. Legally, this is retrieval.
Settle a boundary dispute with {settlement} before it turns into a siege.
Track the {mob} that killed {giver}'s {relative} and bring back its head.
Guide a surveyor through {region} and keep them alive long enough to finish the map.
Buy the {item} back from the {role} in {settlement}, at any price, without haggling.
Find the well that went bad in {region} and find out what is in it.
Collect three months of unpaid tithes from the holdouts in {region}.
Replace the {item}. The original is gone and nobody is to know.
Burn out the {mob} den in {region} and come back before the smoke does.
Sit with the dying {role} until the end, and carry what they say to {settlement}.
Win a drinking contest against the {role}. The town has money on it.
Identify which of the {role}'s three apprentices has been selling to the {mob}.
Carry the {item} to {settlement} on foot. It cannot go on a cart and nobody will say why.
Break {giver}'s {relative} out of the lockup in {settlement} before the hanging.
Count the {mob} in {region}. Precisely. The militia will not move on an estimate.
Return a child who ran off to {region} to join the {mob}.
Drive the {mob} off the grazing land in {region} without killing any of them.
Stand witness at the {role}'s trial in {settlement} and say what you saw.
Find the {item} a previous crawler party was carrying when they went quiet in {region}.
Negotiate safe passage through {region} with whoever is charging for it.
Clear the vermin out of the {role}'s cellar. It is beneath you. It pays.
Deliver {giver}'s {relative} to {settlement} and do not let them talk you out of it.
Recover the {item} from the {mob} that took it, which have begun worshipping it.
Put down the {mob} the {role} has been feeding, before it takes the feeding for granted.
Fetch a healer from {settlement}. Carry them if you have to.
Find out who has been leaving the gates open at night, and why.
Retrieve the {item} from the ruins in {region} before the rains close the road.
Escort a tax collector through {region} and bring the tax collector back as well.
Dig out the pass to {settlement}. The {mob} collapsed it and will do it again.
Serve the {role}'s eviction notice on whatever has moved into {region}.
Sell the {item} in {settlement} for more than it is worth, and do not come back if you cannot.
Bring {giver} proof that the {role} in {settlement} is still alive.
Pull the bodies out of {region} before the {mob} get to them. Names if you can.
Take the {item} to {region} and leave it there. No questions, no explanation.
Scout a new route to {settlement}. The old one goes past the {mob} now.
Settle a debt with the {role} in {settlement}, in coin or in kind.
Find the {mob}'s water source in {region} and foul it.
Guard the {role}'s house for three nights. Something has been trying the door.
Convince the {role} to reopen the shop. The town is rationing.
Walk the {item} through {region} as bait and see what comes for it.
Bring back one of the {mob} alive and in one piece. Nobody will say what for.
Find out what the {role} buried behind {settlement} and whether it is still there.
Hold the bridge at {region} until the refugees from {settlement} are across.
